Introduction

Installation

Install routiva from npm, verify your runtime, and run the bundled demo and test suite.

Requirements#

routiva runs on Node.js 18 or newer and ships as pure ESM. There is no compiler, bundler or transpile step.

RequirementDetail
Node.js18.0.0 or newer ("engines": { "node": ">=18" })
Module systemESM — set "type": "module", or use .mjs files
Runtime dependenciesnone
Dev dependenciesnone
Build stepnone

If your project is CommonJS, add "type": "module" to its package.json and switch require calls to import. routiva ships no CommonJS build.

Install#

bash
npm install routiva

That installs exactly one package. routiva declares no dependencies and no devDependencies, so the install tree is just node_modules/routiva.

Named exports and the default export#

The package has one entry point (src/index.js) with both named and default exports.

Named exports give you the whole toolkit in one import:

js
import { createApp, Router, HttpError, json, serveStatic } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();

The default export is the App class. createApp(options) is simply new App(options):

js
import App from 'routiva';

const app = new App();

The middleware factories are also attached to the class as statics (App.json(), App.logger(), App.serveStatic(), App.rateLimit(), and so on), so this works too:

js
import { App } from 'routiva';

app.use(App.logger());
app.use(App.json());

Print the full export list to confirm what is available:

bash
node -e "import('routiva').then(m => console.log(Object.keys(m).sort().join(' ')))"

Verify your setup#

Create server.js:

js
import { createApp } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();

app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ status: 'ok', node: process.version });
});

app.listen(3000, () => console.log('http://localhost:3000'));
bash
node server.js
curl http://localhost:3000/

You should get back {"status":"ok","node":"v18.x.x"} (your version may differ). If that prints, routing, JSON responses and the HTTP server all work.

Zero dependencies#

No runtime dependencies and no dev dependencies. The test suite is built on node:test and the global fetch, so nothing is installed to run or verify the project.

text
$ npm ls --all
routiva@0.1.2
└── (empty)

That also means faster installs, smaller container images, and a supply-chain surface of exactly one package.

Run the tests#

From a clone of the repository:

bash
node --test          # or: npm test
npm run test:watch   # re-run on change

The suite is 15 test files and 63 tests covering routing, params, request and response APIs, middleware ordering, error propagation, body parsing, cookies, content negotiation, static files, CORS, compression, rate limiting and logging. It starts real HTTP servers on ephemeral ports and makes real requests — there are no mocks.

Run the bundled demo#

The repository ships a complete CRUD app you can run against the source:

bash
npm run crud          # node crud-app/server.js

It listens on port 3000 and serves a browser UI at <http://127.0.0.1:3000> plus a JSON API at /api/products. Override the defaults with environment variables:

bash
PORT=4000 HOST=0.0.0.0 DATA_FILE=./tmp/products.json npm run crud
VariableDefaultPurpose
PORT3000Listening port
HOST127.0.0.1Listening host
DATA_FILEcrud-app/data/products.jsonJSON file used as the datastore

Run the app's integration tests on their own:

bash
npm run crud:test     # node --test crud-app/test/crud.test.js
npm run crud:smoke    # bash crud-app/curl.sh — end-to-end curl script

npm run example runs the smaller examples/basic.js demo instead.

TypeScript#

routiva ships as plain JavaScript with no bundled type declarations and no .d.ts files. With "allowJs": true in your tsconfig.json, TypeScript will import it and infer what it can from the source. Expect some any — there are no generated types yet.

No build step#

package.json points main and exports straight at src/index.js. There is no dist/, no bundler config and no prepare script: the code you import is the code in the repository.
